uncertainObservations: Pole count is NOT reliable and I am recording it as null. Individually resolvable vertical shafts, left to right: (a) one at the extreme left edge; (b) one left-of-center heavily wrapped with blossoms and a ribbon; (c) a thinner one just behind the figure's hair; (d) an upper segment behind/above her head; (e) the one she leans on, running from her hands to the ground; (f) one immediately to her right; (g) one further right; (h) one near the right margin. That reads as six to eight. Items (d) and (e) may be a single continuous pole broken visually by her hands and hair, and items (a) and (c) are faint enough in the mist that either could be a painted tree trunk rather than a staff. I am not confident enough to commit to a number.
Several poles are cut off by the top edge of the artwork, so their full extent is unknown.
Whether the pale strands around her waist are chain, beads or plant stems cannot be determined.
The number of blossoms at lower left cannot be resolved; they overlap heavily.

uncertainObservations: I cannot give a reliable count for the flying blades. Working through them one by one I resolve roughly nine or ten in the upper cluster and roughly nine or ten in the middle cluster, so approximately eighteen to twenty in total — but they overlap, several are very faint against the dark sky, and at least two near the right margin may be cut by the frame edge. uncertainObservations: Disc count is NOT reliable and I record it as null. Along the front/lower ledge I can individually resolve five flat discs in a left-to-right row. Set slightly higher and behind them I can resolve the upright disc under the chisel, and one further disc near the pail at the right. The number of thin tools in the metal pail cannot be counted; roughly four or five rods, heavily overlapping.
Whether the object in her raised hand is a hammer, a mallet or a punch cannot be fully determined, though it reads as a small hammer with a dark head.
The moon's exact phase is obscured by cloud.
The distant skyline cannot be counted into discrete buildings.

uncertainObservations: I cannot reliably count the blades cradled against the shoulder. Two round pommels are clearly and separately resolvable at the top, and I can trace two distinct crossguards and at least two descending blade faces — but the figure's forearm crosses the bundle and there is a further hilt-like shape behind the arm that may be a third blade or may be the edge of one already counted. I record that sub-count as null; it is two or three.
Because of that, the total number of blades in the image is also not something I will commit to — the individually confident sub-counts are: one in the lowered hand, two on the ground.
The two ground blades are partly obscured by grass and the lower one runs close to the border; a third, fully hidden blade in the grass cannot be ruled out, though I see no evidence of one.
The middle-ground figure's sex, and whether either background figure carries anything, cannot be determined at that scale.
The bottom border panel is blank in the artwork itself (not a mask) and carries no readable text.
